A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ZeroGR study and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables and appendices. Renamed datasets and relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original MAIR and BEIR retrieval results and experiments on task diversity, docid design, query volume, model size and decoding.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds docid diagnostics and a controlled query-generator ablation, including results in Appendix F.

M1.justification: The docid generator, instructed query generator, cross-entropy training objective and reverse-annealed retrieval procedure remain unchanged. Expanded Algorithm 1 makes explicit the trie masking and leaf removal already described in v1 Section 4.3; it does not introduce a new procedure.

E1.justification: OpenInstIR corresponds to the existing ZeroGR-Train collection, retaining its six domains and source datasets. Main MAIR and BEIR coverage is unchanged. Additional appendix analyses reuse represented task coverage; newly disclosed development-task lists and query/document types do not establish a coverage expansion. Conflicting task totals do not identify actual dataset additions or removals.

E2.justification: The main MAIR/BEIR comparator sets are unchanged, including GTE-Qwen2-1.5B already present in v1's appendix. v2 adds a doc2query-versus-instructed-query comparison within TIGER (Table 13) and a separate cost comparison using Dense-3B, GENRET-3B and Summary-3B configurations (Table 10).

E3.justification: Retained benchmark metrics and stated generator-training settings remain unchanged. Added protocols include docid-prefix-length analysis, controlled query-generator replacement within TIGER, and cost estimation for a 100K-document corpus with top-1 retrieval, Llama-3B and a single A100 using vLLM. Newly disclosed development-set details do not establish changes to the original experiments.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands component analysis: Figure 4 examines docid collisions versus prefix length and trie branching; Table 13 isolates the query generator's contribution across 25 tasks; Appendix D analyzes computational costs. Tables 5 and 7 add train/evaluation type comparisons and qualitative docid examples. Existing scaling, docid-design and decoding ablations remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, significance tests or comparable uncertainty estimates. Existing boxplots and per-task curves describe task variation; v2 does not introduce statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: The main benchmark values are identical in Table 2 and the corresponding appendix tables, as are retained ablation scores. Substantial new results include a 0.45% eight-word docid conflict rate, estimated indexing/retrieval costs, and Table 13's TIGER comparison: averages of 16.95 with doc2query and 23.35 with the proposed generator, alongside losses such as NFCorpus falling from 41.00 to 6.50. These are additional findings, not improvements over v1's benchmark scores.

T1.justification: The retrieval definitions, docid formulation, training loss, masked sampling distribution and normalized sigmoid schedule are mathematically unchanged. Moving the sampling equation inline and expanding pseudocode introduce no new assumptions, derivations, propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: v2 materially narrows the performance claims: the abstract claims state of the art among generative retrievers, and the introduction describes narrowing the gap to leading dense systems rather than broadly surpassing them. OpenAI performance becomes 'on par.' The existing training collection, renamed OpenInstIR, is also elevated to an explicit dataset contribution in the abstract and contribution list.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly acknowledges underperformance against leading dense retrievers and offers explanations involving training-data overlap and mature dense-retrieval optimization (Appendix C). It adds limitations concerning untested large corpora and larger models, discusses indexing-cost amortization, and interprets docid branching and query-generator effects. These substantially extend and qualify v1's predominantly favorable interpretation.

D1.justification: v2 adds task-resampling thresholds, evaluation sample totals, development-task/query counts and model assignments, beam-size information, baseline checkpoints and configurations, and cost-estimation hardware/runtime details. Figure 6 supplies sigmoid code with default k=10 and m=0.5. These materially expand reproducibility documentation without establishing that previously reported experiments changed.

R1.justification: The related-work framework largely remains intact. v2 adds source-dataset citations, citations for retained GLEN/TIGER baselines, and Wu et al. (2025) on decoding limitations, while removing the instruction-distillation citation by Sun et al. It also explicitly positions OpenInstIR against single-domain or closed training resources. Publication and citation-label updates alone are not substantive changes.

P1.justification: The experimental narrative is substantially reorganized: research questions move into experimental design, ablations precede a separate benchmark-evaluation section, and the appendices are reorganized into seven sections. The abstract, introduction, contribution list and conclusion are revised, related-work subsection headings become paragraph headings, and ZeroGR-Train is renamed throughout.

P2.justification: The unchanged framework diagram moves into the introduction; the BEIR radar chart is replaced by a numerical comparison table; the unseen-MAIR scatterplot and training-data overview graphic are removed. The decoding chart is redrawn horizontally, dataset tables are restructured, and new diagnostic plots, analysis tables and a code display substantially alter the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses important weaknesses in v1's claims and supporting evidence. It aligns the performance narrative with the unchanged gaps to leading dense retrievers, adds controlled evidence for the query generator and diagnostics for docid design, and substantially improves experimental documentation. These strengthen the paper's validity and reproducibility without relying on higher benchmark scores. Dataset-count inconsistencies remain, and the new efficiency numbers are estimates, so the revision does not establish large-scale scalability.
